root_cause.text: The ext4 code incorrectly passed the `EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` flag when splitting an unwritten extent during pre-I/O allocation (with `EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO`), causing `ext4_split_convert_extents()` to mark the entire on-disk extent as written via `EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2`, which led to on-disk/extent status tree inconsistency and stale data exposure if the split failed (e.g., -ENOSPC).
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` flag from the call to `ext4_split_convert_extents()` in `ext4_ext_handle_unwritten_extents()` and adjusts the flag logic so `EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2` is only set when `EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` is present. The commit message details the scenario where failing to split due to -ENOSPC zeroes the first half but converts the entire on-disk extent to written, leaving the second half unwritten in the extent status tree, exposing stale data.

vuln_statements.content: path = ext4_split_convert_extents(handle, inode, map, path, flags | EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT, allocated);

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing handling of EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_UNWRIT_EXT flag to correctly split unwritten extents and only mark data valid when converting to initialized.
intent_record.what: Changed the else-if condition from flag check for EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT to include EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_UNWRIT_EXT via OR; inside the branch, set EXT4_EXT_MARK_UNWRIT2 unconditionally, and conditionally add EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 only when EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT is present.
intent_record.how: The code now also handles the case where only EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_UNWRIT_EXT is set (without EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT) by entering the else-if branch and setting EXT4_EXT_MARK_UNWRIT2 (and possibly EXT4_EXT_MAY_ZEROOUT) but not EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2. Previously this flag combination was not explicitly handled, likely causing missing split behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect flag combination during extent split by not adding EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT unconditionally.
intent_record.what: Changed the flags argument in the call to ext4_split_convert_extents from 'flags | EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT' to 'flags'.
intent_record.how: This removes the forced addition of the EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT flag when splitting extents without merging, so the function now uses only the original flags passed by the caller.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call unconditionally adds EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT when splitting during pre-I/O allocation (with EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO), which causes ext4_split_convert_extents() to mark the entire on-disk extent as written via EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2, leading to on-disk/extent status tree inconsistency and stale data exposure if the split fails (e.g., -ENOSPC).

This line inside ext4_split_convert_extents() unconditionally sets EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 when EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT flag is set, marking the entire on-disk extent as written even during pre-I/O split. If the split fails (e.g., -ENOSPC), the on-disk extent remains incorrectly marked as written, causing inconsistency and potential stale data exposure.
